close_reason: Applied canonical pre-loop string validator at vacation.rs:316-323, matching the fc763f8 pattern from mailbox.rs:878-882. New test vacation_set_destroy_non_string_returns_invalid_arguments asserts invalidArguments on [{}, 1, null]. 251 integration tests pass (was 250).
description:
vacation.rs:316-318 in handle_vacation_set silently continues past non-string entries in the destroy array via 'let id = match id_val.as_str() { Some(s) => s, None => continue, };'. This is the exact antipattern that commit fc763f8 (JMAP-r3pg.18) was supposed to fix uniformly across all 22 *_set handlers in 7 server crates. The fix landed in mailbox.rs, identity.rs, email.rs, submission.rs, sieve.rs (and the corresponding files in chat/calendars/contacts/filenode/sharing/tasks), but vacation.rs was missed.

Trigger: a client sends Vacation/set with {"destroy": [{}, 1, null]}. Per RFC 8620 §5.3 every element of a /set destroy array MUST be a string Id, so the request is malformed and should be rejected with invalidArguments. Current behaviour: the request succeeds with empty destroyed[] and empty notDestroyed; the client has no signal that its request was malformed.

Fix: copy the canonical fc763f8 pattern from mailbox.rs:898-904 into vacation.rs before the for loop at line 315: 'if let Some(bad) = destroy.iter().find(|v| !v.is_string()) { return Err(JmapError::invalid_arguments(...)); }'.
title: vacation.rs destroy silently skips non-string entries
